producer_report.summary:
I added the reconcile step. `athena land` and `athena status` now run it first. It repairs missing landing records from a matching landing intent, or from the host's answer, and otherwise reports the commit as unattributed and writes nothing.

- **Where it lives:** the logic is in `crates/athena-core/src/reconcile.rs`. The host answer comes from a new `GhClient::merged_pr` in `gh.rs`, reached through a `CommitHost` trait.
- **The walk:** it covers main's first-parent commits after the later of the last landing and the first intent's expected base.
- **Skips:** a commit already named by a landing or a declared intervention is skipped.
- **Matching:** an intent matches on head tree and parent. Ambiguity is never guessed. The match rule is `LandingIntent::matches` in `history.rs`.
- **Host fallback:** the host fallback writes a landing only when an intent for that PR with the same head exists.
- **Failures:** a missing records branch, no intent, or any failure becomes a skipped reason or a finding. It never fails the command.
- **Output:** `athena status` shows the findings, including in `--json`. `athena land` prints them to stderr before anything else. `CHANGELOG.md` has the entry.

I ran `cargo test --locked` once and it exited without an error, but its output was too large for me to read the per-test summary. The targeted reconcile tests (6 in core, 2 CLI) passed, and clippy and fmt are clean.

checks_run.note: 6 reconcile tests plus an unrelated name match passed
clean after one fix to a test assertion
Ran once. The command exited without an error code. The output was too large to read here and my tools could not open the saved file, so I did not see the per-test summary.

criteria_check.criterion: Crash repair: a test has a main first-parent commit whose tree and parent match a landing-intent and that has no landing record. Reconcile writes the landing record from the intent alone, with the host making no call. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: reconcile::tests::crash_between_merge_and_landing_is_repaired_from_the_intent_alone passed. It squashes a PR head onto its expected base without a landing record. It asserts one Repaired finding with source Intent, a landing with that host_commit and the intent id, and 0 host calls even though the fake host would error. A second run writes nothing new.

criteria_check.criterion: Host unavailable: a commit with no matching intent and an erroring host gives an 'unattributed' finding and writes no landing record. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: reconcile::tests::unavailable_host_gives_unattributed_and_writes_nothing passed. It asserts an Unattributed finding whose reason contains 'host unavailable', a line containing 'unattributed', no landings, and an unchanged records tip.

criteria_check.criterion: No guessing: a commit with no intent and no merged PR is reported unattributed and nothing is written. It is never attributed to a nearby intent or PR. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: reconcile::tests::no_intent_and_no_pull_request_is_reported_never_guessed passed. Two nearby intents exist. It covers a host answer of none, a PR that has no intent, and a nearby PR with the wrong head. All three are unattributed, with no landing and an unchanged records tip.

criteria_check.criterion: Host fallback: with no matching intent and the host naming the merged PR, the landing record is written for that PR. Commits that already have a landing record are skipped. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: reconcile::tests::host_names_the_merged_pull_request_when_no_intent_matches passed. The intent's base differs from the commit's parent and the host names PR 7. A Repaired finding with source Host is written, with the right intent and host_commit. The host is called once. A landed commit and a declared-intervention commit are not asked about. The landed commit is also skipped by the bound, because it comes before the last landing.

criteria_check.criterion: Bound: commits before the first landing-intent record on athena/records, and before the last landing record, are never reconciled. When the records branch is absent or holds no intent, reconcile does nothing and reports that. A test covers both cases. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: reconcile::tests::bound_skips_older_commits_and_absent_or_empty_records passed. Part A examines only the one commit after the last landing. The host is asked only about it. Older commits, including an unrepaired crashed landing (the known gap), are not examined. Part B has no records branch and Part C has a branch with no intent. Both give a skipped reason, no findings, no host calls and no writes.

criteria_check.criterion: `athena land` and `athena status` run reconcile first, and an unattributed commit appears in their output. A test shows this. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
criteria_check.evidence: crates/athena-cli/tests/reconcile.rs runs the athena binary with a fake gh first on PATH that refuses every call. `status` shows 'unattributed' and the sha on stdout, and `status --json` shows outcome unattributed. `land no-such-job --pr` fails, and its stderr shows the unattributed line first. Both leave no landing written. Both tests passed. Clippy and fmt --check were clean. The full `cargo test --locked` exited without an error code, but I could not read its summary.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry citing docs/design/records-history.md §8.1, D111, and job 3 part 2.
criteria_check.evidence: The first entry under Unreleased cites `docs/design/records-history.md` §8.1 (D111, job 3 part 2). It states the known gap, that a PR merged without an intent stays unattributed, and that declared interventions are read from declared-interventions/. The earlier 'still to do' sentence now points to it.

criteria_check.criterion: The change reuses the existing host and git helpers and record types, adds no dependency, and changes no governance file.
criteria_check.evidence: The code uses GhClient::api with HostOperation::ReadPr, GitLandingRecords and its landing(), LandingFacts, Git helpers, and the HistoryRecord, LandingIntent, Landing and DeclaredIntervention types. No Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow was edited. The build and tests ran with --locked.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: land.rs was not touched, because the reconcile call is in Athena::land_pr in gh.rs. It is listed as a deliverable but was not needed.
Departure from the plan: the display unit test was dropped because building a StatusView by hand is large. The CLI binary tests cover the rendering instead.
Departure from the plan: the CLI test is a new file, crates/athena-cli/tests/reconcile.rs. It uses a fake gh script on PATH with an origin path containing github.com/example/project.git.
Known gap, as planned: an earlier crashed landing that a later landing has passed is not repaired. The user should decide whether criterion 5 should change to cover it.
Declared interventions are read from `declared-interventions/` on the records branch. That directory name is my guess, and nothing writes it yet. Confirm the name or correct it.
A PR merged with no landing intent stays unattributed, because a landing must name its intent. Please confirm this reading of §8.1 step 3.
Rebase merges that replay several commits leave the extra commits unattributed.
`athena status` can now call the host and push to the records branch, so a mostly read-only command has writes. Please confirm this is wanted.
If origin/HEAD is not set locally, reconcile asks the host for the default branch.
mistakes: The first changelog edit failed because the match text was not unique. I redid it with the Unreleased heading as context, and the file is correct.
A clippy lint in my own test code (cloned_ref_to_slice_refs) was fixed after the first clippy run.
I could not read the full `cargo test --locked` output, so I did not see the per-test summary.
learnings: Terminal prints Ui lines to stderr, so `athena land` shows reconcile lines on stderr and `athena status` shows them on stdout in the view.
parse_remote accepts any URL containing `github.com`, so a test origin at `<tmp>/github.com/example/project.git` is accepted. A fake `gh` first on PATH then stands in for the host.

With the walk bounded after the last landing, a commit named by a landing never falls inside the walk. The landed-skip is therefore only a safeguard, and declared-intervention skipping is the case that matters.
The first intent by created_at always has the earliest expected base, because bases only move forward. An abandoned intent therefore cannot widen the walk.
Nothing yet writes declared interventions to the records branch, and the design gives no directory name for them.
desires: A way to read a long test output file inside the working directory, to see the per-test summary of the full run.
The directory name for declared-intervention files on the records branch.
